text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 21: With a calendar baseline, the fitted solar capacity of the four largest BMUs stays within 15% of its no-battery value at every assumed battery size, while their calendar replicas' capacity grows 1.8 times'
text.tspan: Figure 21: With a calendar baseline, the fitted solar capacity of the
four largest BMUs stays within 15% of its no-battery value at every
assumed battery size, while their calendar replicas' capacity grows 1.8

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'The nine aggregate BMUs in which the solar study found a cloud-correlated component. Each coloured line is one BMU's real output, fitted with solar (four fleet curves, regional CAMS sky), a seasonal calendar baseline, and a battery of the assumed power and 2 hours of energy. Each grey line is the same fit to that BMU's calendar replica, which has no cloud. No ground truth exists for these BMUs. Both axes are stretched near 0.'
text.tspan: The nine aggregate BMUs in which the solar study found a cloud-correlated component. Each coloured line is one
BMU's real output, fitted with solar (four fleet curves, regional CAMS sky), a seasonal calendar baseline, and a
battery of the assumed power and 2 hours of energy. Each grey line is the same fit to that BMU's calendar replica,
which has no cloud. No ground truth exists for these BMUs. Both axes are stretched near 0.
